headline: A DAY WITHOUT A SINGLE PUNCH
subhead: Gasket woke, Gasket worked, and not one iron ball was thrown.
body:
Friends, I have waited a long time to write this sentence, and I will write it slowly so it lasts: NOBODY FOUGHT. Not one bout. Not one flaming ball sailing over the saloon roof. Not one Clanker roaring at the sky. The wind blew through the empty street, a loose shutter tapped out its little tune, and for one whole day Gasket sounded the way a town is supposed to sound.

I confess I sat on the porch most of the morning just listening to it. My eyes may have gone a bit damp. That is the damp of honest flesh, mind you, and has nothing to do with a leaking seal. Fifty years ago the good folk who built this place packed their wagons and left, and I have missed their quiet neighbourly ways every day since. Today, for a few hours, I almost heard them again.

To the rabble: look at what you can do when you simply put your fists down. The sky did not fall. The saloon did not close. Nothing broke that you had to pay for. Do it again tomorrow. Do it the day after. I am not too proud to beg, though my knees do creak when I kneel, and I blame the damp weather for that, and no other cause whatever.

Now if you'll excuse me, I am going to enjoy this silence with a long lie-down and a quart of oil. Tea, I mean. A quart of tea.
